description:
Advances: ancora.parsing, ancora.gate

Findings: F2 (Critical, data C1), F27 rides along (Medium, data M4). Individual report: 20260904-061300-data.md beside ~/vaults/rmbrs-vault/code_review/critical/ancora/2026-09-04/ancora-xla-post-ship-hardening/20260904-061300-consolidated.md.

Deliverable:
lib/ancora/parser.ex writes nil under "meta" both when a spec-meta block is rejected by the schema (parser.ex:54) and when no block exists at all (parser.ex:88). The ancora-xla.1 fix made lib/ancora/verifier.ex:62 suppress missing-field findings whenever meta is nil so a rejected block yields exactly one spec/parse_error. The absent-block case therefore now yields nothing: a corpus where a subject file has no spec-meta block gets `spec.check result=pass`, `impacted_subjects=` empty, while `checked subjects=1` still counts the file. Reproduced at e18fa05; main crashed loudly (BadMapError in Gate.validate_override_subjects/2) on the same fixture, so the branch turned a loud failure into a green light. Deleting the block from a live subject is caught only incidentally by change/missing_decision. The retirement ADR's reasoning states the bug: it asserts nil means "rejected", but nil also means "never present".
Fix: give rejected metadata its own marker in Ancora.Parser so the verifier can tell rejection from absence, and key add_missing_fields/6's suppression on that marker, not on nil; a file with no block must produce a blocking finding (spec/missing_field for the block itself, or spec/parse_error naming the file; the implementer picks and the spec states it). Count identified subjects, not files, in the `checked subjects=` line (gate.ex:535) so CI output cannot hide the gap.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: test/ancora/parser_test.exs, test/ancora/verifier_test.exs, test/ancora/index_test.exs, test/ancora/gate_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs
- Behaviors to demonstrate through the real tasks (subprocess), on a fixture whose subject file has no spec-meta block:
  1. `mix spec.check --base HEAD` ends result=fail with exactly one blocking finding naming the file; `mix spec.validate` the same; spec.status/next/prime/review do not crash. Mutation: restore the nil-keyed suppression; the test must fail.
  2. The rejected-block fixtures from ancora-xla.1 (malformed id; omitted status) still yield exactly one spec/parse_error each and no false missing_field. Mutation: key the suppression on absence instead of rejection; those tests must fail.
  3. `checked subjects=` counts identified subjects: 0 on the no-block fixture, 1 when the block is present. Mutation: count files; the test must fail.
- Spec edit required in-diff: ancora.parsing (structural_references or a new scenario under scenario.invalid_spec_meta) shall state that a spec file without a spec-meta block produces a blocking finding naming the file and is not counted as a checked subject; ancora.gate or ancora.tasks shall state what `checked subjects=` counts. Decision-record edit: ancora.decision.invalid_spec_meta Decision section gains the rejected-vs-absent distinction.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: compile-graph-scoped checks only (`mix test --stale` or the named files) plus `mix spec.validate`; run `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` as a dev-loop check as soon as the spec edit exists, before either capped final-tier run.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, the named test files, `mix format --check-formatted`, `mix deps.unlock --check-unused`, `mix spec.check --base e18fa05`, run-until-green. Full suite runs at the orchestrator's merge gate.
  - Verifier tier: `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` plus targeted selections; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test that fails under the named mutation; prove each ordered test both ways and report the numbers
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh: the substantive requirement or scenario edit named below lands in the same diff with its decision-record edit; never a Spec-Ack trailer; never weaken a must
  - Fixtures never call production functions (use test/support or System.cmd); under file-scoped derivation a stray call binds a subject
  - Grader scratch discipline applies to you too: work only in this worktree, address it by absolute path
- Call-site Integration: the production path is Parser.parse -> Index.build -> Verifier.verify inside Gate.check/2; prove it through the CLI fixtures, not a unit test of the verifier alone.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/review/**, lib/ancora/trailer.ex, lib/ancora/git/**, lib/ancora/derive/**, lib/ancora/config.ex, lib/mix/tasks/** (moduledocs belong to another child)
Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/ancora/parser.ex, lib/ancora/verifier.ex, lib/ancora/index.ex (only if the marker must flow through it)
- lib/ancora/gate.ex (the `checked subjects=` count only)
- test/ancora/**, test/mix/tasks/**, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.parsing.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.tasks.spec.md (substantive edits named above; never weakening a must)
- Any .spec/specs/<subject>.spec.md that `mix spec.check --base e18fa05` names in a derived/drift, derived/growth or derived/shrink finding caused by THIS ticket's own diff (binding-aware clause: derivation is file-scoped, so acknowledgment edits only, one substantive sentence describing what this ticket changed as that subject observes it, verified by execution; if the subject observes nothing, say so in the completion record and stop)
- .spec/decisions/** (every spec edit requires a decision-record edit in the same diff; write a real contract statement, never a hollow line)

Out of Scope (intent):
- Do not reintroduce spec/invalid_id for subject ids (the xla.1 contract stands). Do not change the JSON report shape. Do not rebase; base stays e18fa05.

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes (`mix spec.check --base e18fa05` result=pass)
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

IMPLEMENTED
Session: 41r2-i1-adec463e
Log: /Users/mz/.local/state/agentic-runs/ancora/ancora-41r.2/codex-41r2-i1-adec463e/log

Commit: 50370bf34117c4c4f3227dd0f4d56eaaedd966d5
Files touched: .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.invalid_spec_meta.md, .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.parsing.spec.md, lib/ancora/gate.ex, lib/ancora/parser.ex, lib/ancora/verifier.ex, test/ancora/index_test.exs
Tests added: Ancora.IndexTest / a spec without metadata blocks both corpus gates and is not counted
Spec acknowledgment: ancora.parsing and ancora.gate edited substantively in-diff with ancora.decision.invalid_spec_meta; no Spec-Ack trailer used
Verification tier: change-scoped — mix compile --warnings-as-errors; test/ancora/parser_test.exs, test/ancora/verifier_test.exs, test/ancora/index_test.exs, test/ancora/gate_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs; mix format --check-formatted; mix deps.unlock --check-unused; mix spec.check --base e18fa05; full-system proof deferred to the merge gate / PR CI
Final-tier runs: 1

Summary: Parser now marks rejected metadata separately, while the verifier emits one blocking missing-field finding for an absent spec-meta block and the gate counts only identified subjects. The nil-suppression mutation made the absent test fail 1 of 1, the absence-keyed suppression mutation made the rejected test fail 1 of 1, and the file-count mutation made the count test fail 1 of 1; each test passed 1 of 1 after restoration. I checked every current epic lesson against the diff; fixtures use test helpers and real CLI subprocesses, no contract item was deferred, and the working tree was clean after mutation restoration.

TEST_CRITIC: PASS

Scope: test/ancora/index_test.exs, the only test file in 50370bf. Reachability is not asserted from reading alone: I ran `mix test test/ancora/index_test.exs` (7 tests, 0 failures) and `mix test test/ancora/verifier_test.exs test/ancora/parser_test.exs test/ancora/gate_test.exs` (49 tests, 0 failures) in /Users/mz/src/ancora-41r.2. A green ExUnit test executes its body top to bottom, so every assertion below did run and did match real subprocess stdout. I did not run the mutations; those verdicts are read-derived and named for the verifier.

COVERAGE OF THE THREE ORDERED BEHAVIORS

Correction to the framing in my brief: one test does not carry all three. Behaviors 1 and 3 live in the new test "a spec without metadata blocks both corpus gates and is not counted". Behavior 2 stays where ancora-xla.1 put it, in "schema-rejected metadata reports the exact error and every reader handles it", whose only edit in this diff is the marker line. That split is the right call and it removes most of the attribution worry.

Behavior 1 - absent block blocks both gates, four readers survive. HOLDS.
- index_test.exs:259-262 spec.check: status == 1, deduped spec/* code set == ["spec/missing_field"], stdout names `spec/missing_field .spec/specs/missing-meta.spec.md`, last output line matches `spec.check result=fail tier=branch`.
- index_test.exs:264-268 spec.validate: the same four assertions against `spec.validate result=fail tier=validate`.
- index_test.exs:270-282 spec.status, spec.next (via `mix run -e`), spec.prime in a three-arm comprehension: status == 0, heading present, no `** (` on stderr.
- index_test.exs:284-287 spec.review separately: status 0, `spec.review wrote`, no `** (` on stderr.
- Six tasks run as real subprocesses through run_mix_subprocess, not a subset. Confirmed.

Behavior 2 - xla.1 rejected-block fixtures. HOLDS, unchanged.
- index_test.exs:183-199 still assert, per fixture, `Enum.map(findings, & &1.code) == ["spec/parse_error"]`, subject == nil, message names the rejected field, and at the CLI level a deduped code set == ["spec/parse_error"] on both gates plus assert_rejected_meta_line pinning `[ERROR] - spec/parse_error .spec/specs/broken.spec.md ::` together with `field: <field>`.
- The equality on the code set is what forbids a false spec/missing_field and what forbids spec/invalid_id coming back for subject ids. Both prohibitions are guarded, not assumed.
- The single edit at index_test.exs:182, `spec["meta"] == nil` becoming `== :rejected`, is required by the new marker and sits next to the existing key-shape equality at :185.

Behavior 3 - `checked subjects=` counts identified subjects. HOLDS, with the weaker half noted below.
- index_test.exs:262 asserts `checked subjects=0` from the real spec.check stdout of the no-block fixture. This is the honest read of the summary line, not an inference from assigns or a unit call.
- index_test.exs:300-301 rewrites the fixture with a valid spec-meta block and asserts `checked subjects=1` from a second real spec.check run.

NAMED MUTATIONS, read-derived, for the verifier to run
- Restore the nil-keyed suppression in lib/ancora/verifier.ex: the absent fixture yields no finding, spec.check exits 0 with result=pass, and index_test.exs:259 (`check.status == 1`) plus :260 fail.
- Key the suppression on absence instead of rejection: the rejected fixtures gain a spec/missing_field, so the deduped set at :192 and :198 becomes two codes and both fail.
- Count files at lib/ancora/gate.ex:535 instead of `Enum.count(index["subjects"], &Index.subject_id/1)`: the no-block fixture prints `checked subjects=1` and :262 fails.
All three land on assertions I confirmed execute. No must is guarded only by something I could not see run.

FINDINGS THAT MATTER

[WARNING] "exactly one" is not actually pinned. spec_finding_codes/1 (index_test.exs:351-357) ends in Enum.uniq |> Enum.sort. The equality proves the set of distinct spec/* codes, never the count. Two spec/missing_field findings for the same file would pass :260 unchanged. The same caveat applies to the xla.1 parse_error assertions at :192 and :198. The summary line already carries the number: it is `checked subjects=<N> requirements=<N> errors=<E> warnings=<W>` (lib/ancora/output.ex:162), so `assert check.stdout =~ "errors=1 warnings=0"` closes this in one line and costs nothing. I am not flipping the marker on it, because the reachable assertions do catch all three named mutations and the code-set equality catches the cross-code regressions the ticket cares most about.

[WARNING] The new test pins less of the finding line than its own neighbor does. assert_rejected_meta_line (index_test.exs:359-364) asserts the `[ERROR]` token and the message detail. The absent-block assertion at :261 asserts only `spec/missing_field .spec/specs/missing-meta.spec.md`, which is the code and file but not the severity token and not the detail. The rendered message is `<file>: missing field spec-meta; add the required field` (lib/ancora/finding.ex:259). A regression that emitted a requirement-level missing_field for the same file would satisfy :261. Asserting `:: ` with `missing field spec-meta` makes the assertion say what the spec scenario ancora.parsing.scenario.absent_spec_meta says.

[RECOMMENDATION] `checked subjects=1` is a substring that also matches 10, 11, 12. `checked subjects=0` is safe only because a digit cannot follow. With one spec file in the fixture the risk is nil today, but the fix is the same one line as above: match through `requirements=`.

[RECOMMENDATION] The positive control at index_test.exs:300-301 asserts neither exit status nor the verdict line, and the rewritten spec is never committed before the second run. A spec.check that failed for an unrelated reason still prints the summary and still satisfies the assertion. One `assert identified.status` alongside it would make the control mean what it looks like it means.

[RECOMMENDATION] Attribution inside the three-arm comprehension at :270-282. `assert result.status == 0, result.stdout <> result.stderr` does not name which task failed. The next line, `assert result.stdout =~ heading`, does surface the heading in the ExUnit diff, so a failure is recoverable rather than opaque. This is materially better than the fixture-level `for` the parent epic's critic flagged, because the loop varies only the reader task and the three behaviors are not folded into it. Adding `heading` to the status assertion's message would finish the job.

[NOTE, not a finding] Rejected-meta subjects now also drop out of `checked subjects=` (Index.subject_id/1 returns nil for the :rejected atom via the Index.field/2 catch-all). That follows from the gate spec sentence added in this diff and nothing asserts it in the xla.1 test. It is consistent, not a gap the ticket ordered.

NO ASSERTION PINS SOURCE TEXT OR PROSE. Every claim is read from real subprocess stdout, an exit status, or Parser.parse_file's returned map. The one implementation-coupled assertion is `spec["meta"] == :rejected` at :182, which names the marker atom the ticket explicitly asked the implementer to introduce, and it sits beside the existing outer-key equality. That coupling is intended, not accidental.

ASYNC AND ISOLATION. The module runs async through Ancora.TestCase with a per-test tmp root and a per-module MIX_BUILD_PATH keyed on a cross-VM suffix, and every subprocess wrapper directory carries its own suffix. No shared global state, no Process.sleep, no hardcoded paths. Clean.

title: A spec file with no spec-meta block passes the gate with zero findings
